title: Eneco says Belgium's cybersecurity centre told it customer data was apparently stolen; thousands of records
date_note: RTBF's page shows only 'Il y a 3 heures' (3 hours ago) and no absolute date; the day is taken as the day it was read, 26 November. RTBF says the data was taken the previous weekend.
geo_basis: country; RTBF describes Eneco as a Belgian energy supplier
summary: RTBF, VRT and ITdaily report that Belgium's Centre for Cybersecurity (CCB) told Eneco that customer data had apparently been stolen, after Eneco first denied a hack. ITdaily says Eneco lists address, IBAN, BIC and EAN code as taken and dates the incident 25 November; Eneco says the problem is fixed. RTBF says a hacker's larger claim is unverified.
plain: Energy supplier Eneco says thousands of customers' bank account numbers and addresses were apparently stolen. A hacker claims far more, which is unverified. Eneco says it will inform customers.
exec: Eneco says thousands of customer bank account numbers and postal addresses were apparently stolen, and a hacker claims a larger number that is unverified.
action: Eneco advises staying alert to phishing: it says it never asks for PIN codes, passwords, itsme or verification codes, and its emails come from eneco.be or eneco.com.

validation.note: RTBF, VRT and ITdaily (independent publishers) each report Eneco's statement that the CCB told it customer data was apparently stolen; Eneco's own notice not read.

review.note: stronger than the source: RTBF quotes Eneco conditionally (auraient été dérobées); now says apparently stolen
